blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The House of Representatives on Thursday passed on final reading a bill modernizing the country’s anti-espionage laws, despite lawmakers’ concerns that its broad definition of spying could be used to crack down on dissent. With 224 lawmakers voting for House Bill No. 9642 and 10 against, the lower chamber approved the measure, which expands espionage to cover the sharing of any “classified matter” in times of peace or war if its disclosure could harm the country by giving an advantage to foreign or domestic actors.
